"It is marvelous, Blessed One, how this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya is endowed with such eloquence... [13 akṣaras missing] ... capable, [8 akṣaras missing] ... a teacher, and how he is a teacher of the Dharma through profound words, and a teacher of the Dharma through connected words."

"Furthermore, Ānanda, it is not that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya is now praising me face-to-face with verses. Rather, Ānanda, in the past, in a time long gone, when ten incalculable eons had been completed, at that time and on that occasion, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Jyotivikrīḍitābhijña—one endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans."
The Buddha is the Blessed One.
Now at that time, Ānanda, there was a young brahmin named Bhadraśuddha, who was handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold, endowed with the most excellent and abundant splendor of complexion.

Then, while standing in the midst of the marketplace, he beheld that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jyotirvikrīḍitābhijña— whose faculties were tranquil, whose mind was peaceful, who had attained the supreme perfection of the highest self-control and tranquility, who was like a dragon with conquered senses, as clear, serene, and untroubled as a lake, rising up like a golden sacrificial pillar, radiant, glowing, and shining with glory, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man.

Then, having seen him, this thought occurred to him: "How wonderful! To what an extent this divine body of the Tathāgata blazes—blazing with color, blazing with splendor, blazing with glory, and blazing with the primary marks! Then the brahmin youth Bhadraśuddha said: "O, may I too blaze in just this way—with color, splendor, glory, and the primary marks! Then it occurred to the brahmin youth Bhadraśuddha: "What if I were to manifest myself before the Blessed One? And at that very moment...

Having fallen upon the earth, this thought occurred to him: "If, in a future time, I might become such as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jyotirvikrīḍitābhijña, may this Tathāgata touch me with his two feet."

Then, Ānanda, the Tathāgata Jyotivikrīḍitābhijña, having known with his own mind the reflection in the mind of the young brahmin Bhadraśuddha, approached where the young brahmin Bhadraśuddha was; having approached, he touched the body of the young brahmin Bhadraśuddha with his two feet.

Furthermore, Ānanda, as soon as the Tathāgata Jyotivikrīḍitābhijña touched the body of the brahmin boy Bhadraśuddha with his two feet, at that very moment he attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Then, Ānanda, the Tathāgata Jyotivikrīḍitābhijña looked back and addressed the community of monks.
Furthermore, monks, no one at all should touch the body of this brahmin boy Bhadraśuddha with their feet. Why is that? Because he will become a Tathāgata in a future time.

Then, Ānanda, at that very moment, they obtained the divine eye born from the maturation of past karma; they obtained the divine ear born from the maturation of past karma, knowledge of the minds of others, recollection of former abodes, and the miraculous power of transformations.
Then, Ānanda, from that point on for the brahmin boy Bhadraśuddha—[the rest is almost completely lost].
